invariants.rationale: Cursors in Java text editing contexts are typically non-negative, representing a position in the string.
Selection start index in text editors should be non-negative, corresponding to a valid string index.
If a selection exists, its start should not be after the cursor, which is a common invariant for text selections.
Text should not be null at the start of this method, as it is likely required by subsequent operations.
Cursor should not exceed the text length; if text is null, treat length as 0 for safety.
